description: Out-of-distribution robustness check: COCO (real, label=0) vs DALLE-3 (fake, label=1), clean vs transformed. AUC computed with sklearn.metrics.roc_auc_score on raw 'pred' (P(fake)) scores. Two versions below -- read the 'label' field on each before quoting a number.

balanced_subsampled.label: BALANCED -- real images randomly subsampled to match the fake count, so clean and transformed use the same real:fake ratio and accuracy is directly comparable between them.
balanced_subsampled.method: COCO's 4,996 real predictions randomly subsampled (random.seed(42), Python stdlib `random.sample`) down to 1,808 to match della.json's fake count. Transformed set (coco_transformed.json / della_transformed.json) was already balanced 2,000/2,000 and used as-is.

full_imbalanced.label: IMBALANCED -- full prediction sets, unmodified. Clean is 4,996 real / 1,808 fake (73/27 split); transformed is 2,000/2,000 (50/50). Kept for reference / auditability, NOT for a clean-vs-transformed accuracy comparison.
full_imbalanced.method: All available predictions used as originally run, no subsampling.

robustness_gap.note: Accuracy here is NOT directly comparable between clean and transformed -- clean is 73/27 real:fake, transformed is 50/50, so accuracy at a fixed threshold is confounded by class balance alone. AUC is still valid (threshold-free). This is why the balanced_subsampled block above exists.
